option: Confirm exactly what the paid offer commits to
evidence: Local offer promises all future digital content and permanent membership grandfathering; live site describes a different bundle and future discount. These are material ongoing commitments.
first_step: Create a plain inclusion list: available now, promised later, updates, print terms, access method and existing buyer commitments. CT confirms it before copy changes.
done_when: One authoritative offer drives pages, policies and customer messages; no silent repricing or withdrawal of prior commitments.

option: Verify access and delivery from beginning to end
evidence: The site promises immediate delivery. Recent daily notes record an account quota problem and an unconfirmed sender lead; a successful CI run does not prove delivery.
first_step: Establish current sender/account status, then run an authorized test flow with a designated recipient and record payment, access and correct-download outcomes.
done_when: One dated acceptance record for success and recoverable failure, with the right edition delivered.

option: Choose one manuscript and release baseline
evidence: PR24 integrates v0.11.0; PR26 is a separate core-cut document; PR27 adds a foreword to older main. These are not interchangeable editions.
first_step: Write a one-page inclusion decision: public edition, working edition, source commit, foreword destination, and deferred proposals.
done_when: One unambiguous source/manifest for the next edition and an explicit inclusion list.

option: Align the public promise and access language
evidence: Live homepage still sells individual escape; v0.11.0 defines collective survival. Live navigation describes open reading while /book requires a purchase-email password.
first_step: Compare hero, survival block, navigation, Introduction and purchase page. CT chooses the promise; implement one consistent description.
done_when: A newcomer can explain the book's purpose and access conditions without prompting.

option: Settle the opening, voice and ending decisions
evidence: Core critique flags multiple openings; voice history preserves author passages and identifies cut material. The new foreword introduces another opening choice.
first_step: Prepare a short decision packet: opening order, foreword role, retained author passages, narrative register and closing invitation.
done_when: CT approves a provisional editorial brief for the reader-session candidates; reader findings then inform the final brief.

option: Run five focused reader sessions
evidence: Existing reader proofs check rendering. AI critiques identify hypotheses, not demonstrated reader comprehension or demand.
first_step: Use a provisional opening and one practical passage with five relevant readers. Ask what the book promises, where they stop, and what action they can take.
done_when: Five recorded sessions with recurring problems, counterexamples and decisions; no statistical market claim.

option: Audit the claims retained in the chosen text
evidence: v0.11.0 checked new additions, not every inherited claim. Public statistics and causal forecasts still need passage-specific evidence.
first_step: Prioritize the homepage statistics, causal/forecast claims, comparisons and practical prescriptions. Reuse block IDs and the citation trail.
done_when: Each high-impact claim has a bounded verdict and source locator, or is revised/removed with author review.

option: Pilot one author-led chapter rewrite
conditions: Ratings cover one chapter pilot. Full-manuscript expansion is a separate author decision after the pilot; its effort is not scored here.
evidence: PR26 supplies 50,469 verbatim words, 2,178 block decisions and 196 seams. It is preparation for CT's v0.12 rewrite, not finished prose.
first_step: Rewrite one representative chapter using the core cut, voice decisions and reader findings. Agents prepare evidence and track seams.
done_when: CT accepts the pilot and its reader test; use its budget and method for later chapters.

option: Repair the release checks and diagnose WebKit failures
evidence: PR24 has failed WebKit, mobile Safari and tablet jobs. Some older tests assert only if a feature exists; one accepts zero revealed elements.
first_step: Inspect the failed test reports, remove stale-route assumptions and make relevant checks fail on intentionally broken fixtures.
done_when: Relevant checks detect their intended defect, then pass on the release candidate. Failure causes are classified, not inferred from red status.

option: Match the reader, downloads and bundle to one edition
evidence: PR24 reader is v0.11.0 while downloads remain v0.7.5. Its 42.5 MB reading PDF exceeds the candidate's documented static-file limit. Local bundle manifest also names v0.7.5.
first_step: Select the deliverable edition, reuse the build pipeline, choose suitable file size/hosting, and compare metadata and hashes across access paths.
done_when: Reader, PDF, EPUB and bundle clearly identify the intended edition, with working links and hosting-compatible files.

option: Test one practical activity or companion guide
conditions: Ratings cover one bounded activity pilot. A full companion or many new instructions require a later scope decision.
evidence: Appendix material and field-manual rules are reusable, while critique questions whether several chapter titles deliver practical instruction.
first_step: Pick one bounded low-cost activity with real inputs, labor, limitations and observed result; decide whether it belongs in the book or companion.
done_when: A reader can complete the activity and identify its limits; the example informs the book's practical promise.

option: Integrate the already measured website corrections
evidence: Three commits preserve rendering, labels, dates, metadata and audit tools. Prior local measurements show improvements; production HTML still lacks factcheck body content.
first_step: Review the three commits on the selected release base and re-run their focused served-page acceptance checks.
done_when: Correct content, labels, dates and metadata survive the integration on the served build.

option: Resolve the foreword's sources and wording decisions
conditions: Primary-source collection can start immediately. Inclusion and placement require D01 and D07.
evidence: PR27 records primary-source gaps, softened dictated claims and a proposed sign-off. Its foreword is not yet a built edition.
first_step: Check primary DARPA, UN and project documents; present only the remaining factual and author choices.
done_when: Accepted foreword has supported/bounded factual claims and explicit placement in the selected edition.

option: Regenerate the public evidence trail against the selected source
evidence: Factcheck/workshop outputs can be stale and their receipts depend on origin/main. Archive presence alone does not satisfy the existing receipt policy.
first_step: Build against the intended publication commit; distinguish unchecked evidence from unresolved Git receipts. Refresh the public trace after integration.
done_when: Displayed claims, source locators, counts and receipt statuses match the published edition.

option: Run one video or excerpt distribution experiment
conditions: A sales CTA requires D03 and D10. A free excerpt seeking feedback can run earlier once its wording and sources are ready; it need not wait for a paid release.
evidence: PR20 has 21 scripts with Shorts, sources and CTA ideas. Pixel project has Chapter 15 videos, but older captions and rights require review.
first_step: Choose one script or excerpt, one existing channel and one reader action. Check claims/rights and record a modest outcome target before publishing.
done_when: Measure qualified replies, excerpt visits and completed reader actions; use results to decide a second piece.

option: Extract a source-derived public ledger or sample
conditions: A genuinely free sample does not require paid fulfillment. Email-gated access requires a working delivery route and coherent access terms.
evidence: PR20 already extracts precedent prose from canonical Markdown. It expects 23 precedents while v0.11.0 has 24.
first_step: Isolate the route, update its extraction checks and decide free/sample/email access coherently with the offer.
done_when: A useful public sample draws from current source without duplicate prose or a misleading access promise.

option: Source or narrow the three unsourced bundle cases
conditions: Research can begin now. Final manifest and displayed claims must be reconciled with D10 before shipping an updated bundle.
evidence: Local bundle manifest records 31 cases and 28 with sources, naming B1, C4 and D2 as missing. This count is distinct from the book's precedent count.
first_step: Review those three cases and add primary evidence or narrow/label the claims; rebuild the manifest from the actual bundle.
done_when: Every claim has an honest evidence status, and displayed counts agree with the delivered file.

option: Complete final digital and physical publication proofs
conditions: D11 applies only if the foreword is included; D12 applies only for a rewritten edition. Physical proofs and vendor requirements apply only to a print release. Interim digital release remains an option.
evidence: v0.11.0 has EPUB/PDF proofs, text/geometry checks and portable sources. It still lacks complete rights/physical-print acceptance and dedicated-reader proof.
first_step: Once text/art settles, use the existing production machinery; obtain device and print proofs appropriate to the chosen channels.
done_when: Edition-specific acceptance record covers text, images, device behavior, physical print and distribution requirements.

option: Replace conflicting current-status documentation with a thin index
evidence: Current-status documents still describe free/open access and unimplemented preorder. Edition labels also refer to different branches and releases.
first_step: Keep history intact, label superseded pages and link one source/edition/release/decision index after CT chooses the baseline.
done_when: A collaborator can locate current source, public offer, release candidate and blockers from one page.

option: Use the existing local manuscript search tool
evidence: PR22 implements lexical search over stable manuscript block IDs and a localhost interface. Generated answers are optional and were not exercised.
first_step: Port the lexical search to the chosen source and try real editorial queries with known relevant passages.
done_when: Editing questions return useful source passages and stable IDs; adopt only if it saves actual retrieval effort.

option: Finish local fonts and click-to-load video work
evidence: Active site work already contains fonts, licenses, fetcher and lazy video changes. New LiteYouTube and compare_tiles edits appeared after the archive cutoff.
first_step: Let the current work stabilize, review its diff and use the existing network and scrolled-tile tools.
done_when: Arrival requests/bytes and visual changes are recorded; video loads on activation and controls remain usable.

option: Adapt the labor-hour essay as a standalone piece
evidence: PR21 contains a blog essay and book insertions targeting an older manuscript. The branch names remaining voice and link checks.
first_step: Review the essay alone, preserve its source corrections, and select a clear reader question before integrating any chapter material.
done_when: One supported essay fits the chosen public promise; book additions remain a separate editorial decision.

option: Keep preservation incremental as active work changes
evidence: Complete archive coverage was verified through 06:15 PDT. Later active edits and plain-claims commit 396b238 show why backup claims need a cutoff.
first_step: After each owned milestone, record source commits and snapshot only new authored work. Keep archive branches separate from release candidates.
done_when: Each completed milestone has a recoverable GitHub location and timestamped coverage, without another broad backup project.

option: Evaluate the game as a separate teaching prototype
evidence: Shouse game has an engine, HUD and simulation assets, but older cost, income, permit and route assumptions. Current playability is unverified.
first_step: Only after reader evidence identifies a teaching need, test a single scenario and audit its assumptions.
done_when: Readers learn one intended concept without mistaking game assumptions for practical forecasts.

option: Undertake a broad visual redesign
evidence: Useful components and audit tools already exist. Known clarity, delivery and testing defects give narrower work a stronger basis.
first_step: Make only changes tied to observed reader/task failures; preserve historical MVP components as optional references.
done_when: A specific observed task improves, with no regression in access or clarity.

option: Expand membership or other platform features
evidence: Offer already makes future membership commitments, but this assessment contains no evidence of membership demand or operating capacity.
first_step: Define the obligation and test the need with existing readers before adding account, community or subscription workflows.
done_when: A specific reader need, sustainable operating plan and agreed scope precede implementation.

option: Build a production tracker only after recurring production exists
evidence: Existing production-tracker is a Svelte scaffold with no implemented tracking workflow. One pilot does not require a new platform.
first_step: Use a simple production table for the first pilots; identify repeated coordination failures before building software.
done_when: A documented recurring workflow justifies software beyond a shared table.
